submission.justification: Recommend Absorber-F3 with 5.5 mm plates. The project documents list F3 as an allowed candidate absorber and note that the mechanical support is compatible with every absorber candidate, with common cooling/readout interfaces. Simulation scans over the full allowed 2--10 mm interval showed F3 gives the best 100 GeV electron energy resolution among the three materials; a fine scan around the minimum found 5.5 mm to be the best sampled thickness. Repeated 100k-event simulations at 5.5 mm gave results around 3.05--3.21%, averaging about 3.12%, lower than the best sampled F2 point (~3.7--3.9%) and F1 point (~5.0%).

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV.
requirements.evidence: Full material/thickness scan plus fine scan identified Absorber-F3 as the lowest-resolution material; repeated simulations at 5.5 mm returned 3.204, 3.079, 3.127, 3.103, 3.090, 3.069, 3.209, and 3.049% at 100 GeV, averaging approximately 3.12%, better than the sampled minima for F2 and F1.

requirements.requirement: The absorber must be one of the three materials listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Absorber-F1, Absorber-F2, and Absorber-F3; the recommendation selects Absorber-F3.

requirements.requirement: The calorimeter must allow hands-on maintenance during shutdowns.
requirements.evidence: No project document identifies a maintenance-access or activation disqualifier for Absorber-F3. The 2026-05-14 meeting notes state the mechanical support design is compatible with every candidate absorber, and cooling/readout documents state those systems are common to all absorber options.
The recommended plate thickness is 5.5 mm, within the allowed 2--10 mm range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended material and plate thickness.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one final recommendation: Absorber-F3 at 5.5 mm.
